name: Germany
dek: Berlin-Tempelhof as the capital station. Not a national average. Munich and Frankfurt are different tables.
paragraphs: The table is Berlin-Tempelhof, WMO 10384, at 47.7 m. Berlin-Dahlem and Berlin-Brandenburg are separate complete files. They are not averaged with Tempelhof. Germany does not have one climate, and this page does not invent a national mean.

Munich and Frankfurt have their own sheets. Tempelhof's winter minimums are below zero and its summer highs are in the mid-twenties. Munich's city station is higher and colder. The plug, the road rule, and the tourist office's tipping line are national and are repeated on the city sheets. Büsingen is the other time zone in the IANA file and it is not one of these sheets.

climate.caption: Reference station: Berlin-Tempelhof, WMO 10384. Not a national average.
climate.note: World Meteorological Organization 1991–2020 climatological standard normals, distributed by NOAA NCEI. The file prints some values without a leading zero, including negatives such as -.4. Those tokens are copied as printed.

plugs.label: Plugs and voltage
plugs.value: Type C and F, 230 V, 50 Hz
plugs.detail: The IEC world-plugs list shows Germany at 230 volts and 50 hertz, with plug types C and F.

driving.label: Driving side
driving.detail: Section 2 of the Straßenverkehrs-Ordnung says vehicles must use the carriageways, and where there are two carriageways they must use the right one. The next paragraph says to drive as far to the right as possible, not only when there is oncoming traffic, when being overtaken, at crests, in curves, or where the view is unclear. Later sections allow marked multi-lane roads to depart from that rightward rule in the cases they name.

tipping.label: Tipping
tipping.detail: The German National Tourist Office resource guide, released in September 2025, says restaurant bills include VAT and service charges, and that a 10 percent tip is common. Berlin.de's own tipping page describes service as usually not included and gives a wider range. Those two pages are not averaged. This sheet uses the national guide.
tipping.sourceTitle: German National Tourist Office, resource guide (September 2025)

water.label: Tap water
water.detail: CDC's traveler page for Germany, last reviewed 25 August 2026, does not say whether tap water is safe or unsafe. It says food and water standards around the world vary based on the destination, that standards may also differ within a country, and that risk may change depending on the activity. It points readers to CDC's food and water precautions. This page does not turn that into medical advice.

currency.label: Currency
currency.detail: ISO 4217 lists the currency name Euro and the code EUR for Germany.

timeZone.label: Time zone
timeZone.detail: IANA's zone1970.tab gives Europe/Berlin the comment most of Germany. The other German row in that file is Büsingen, on Europe/Zurich. Berlin, Munich, and Frankfurt are not Büsingen.

entry.label: Official entry requirements
entry.note: The foreign office's visa overview. We do not restate a visa rule.
